title: Exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
formal: Determine the asymptotic worst-case expected approximation ratio of Best Fit bin packing when an adversary chooses the item multiset and its arrival order is uniformly random.
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Define the asymptotic supremum over instances, tie breaking and additive terms; the default numerical benchmark tolerance is distinct from exact identification of the ratio.
answer_criterion: Supply a real approximation to the defined optimal constant and a Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most \(1/100\). Exact determination also qualifies; the approximation does not establish an associated exact conjecture. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. Pending: Define the asymptotic supremum over instances, tie breaking and additive terms; the default numerical benchmark tolerance is distinct from exact identification of the ratio.
context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Claire Mathieu. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: The target measures how much a random arrival order improves a classical greedy packing rule.

import_provenance.original_title: The exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
import_provenance.original_statement: An adversary chooses the item multiset, then its order is uniformly randomly permuted before Best Fit packs it. Determine the asymptotic worst-case expected ratio to OPT; the conjectured value near 1.15 is still separated substantially from the upper bound.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Beating 3/2 is already resolved: the 2024 result gives 1.5−ε for a fixed ε>0 and a lower bound of 1.144. The open problem here is the true ratio.
